elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) expressly permits Sparkling to assign the Agreement to an affiliate without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with a merger.
elements.evidence: Section (d) permits assignment without consent to a successor in connection with a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section (d) permits assignment without consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with a sale of all or substantially all of its assets.
elements.evidence: Section (d) permits assignment without consent to a successor in connection with a sale of all or substantially all of Sparkling's assets or business.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign this Agreement without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence of Section (d) requires Garman to obtain Sparkling's written consent before assigning the Agreement or its rights and obligations.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The required consent expressly may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Section (d) categorically states that Garman may not assign the Agreement to a competitor of Sparkling.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement because of a change of control of Customer.
elements.evidence: Section (d) states that a change of control of Sparkling does not constitute an assignment and gives Garman no right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Sparkling may assign without consent to a successor in connection with the broadly listed merger, amalgamation, acquisition, reorganization, or sale transactions.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice when assigning this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Sparkling's permitted successor assignment is expressly conditioned on written notice to Garman.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: No successor carve-out is provided for Garman; all Garman assignments remain subject to Sparkling's consent.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice when assigning this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: The clause provides neither a notice-based successor assignment right nor a corresponding written-notice mechanism for Garman.

elements.element: Customer may make assignments other than successor assignments with Vendor's consent, and may not make them without that consent.
elements.evidence: Sparkling may assign to an affiliate without consent even where the affiliate is not a successor, so Vendor consent is not required for every non-successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to Customer assignments for which consent is required may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence applies the prohibition on unreasonably withholding or delaying consent to either party's required consent.

elements.element: Vendor may make assignments other than successor assignments with Customer's consent, and may not make them without that consent.
elements.evidence: Although Sparkling's consent is generally required, Garman is absolutely prohibited from assigning to a Sparkling competitor even if Sparkling were to consent; therefore not all such assignments can be made through the consent mechanism.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The general reasonableness standard is operative for permitted Garman assignments, but the absolute competitor prohibition removes that category from any effective consent process, contrary to a reasonableness-based consent regime for all other assignments.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement, including Customer's affiliate and transaction-successor carve-outs, the reasonableness standard for Vendor assignments, the competitor prohibition, and the exclusion of Vendor termination rights upon Customer change of control. It does not satisfy the mutual fallback because Vendor receives no notice-only successor assignment right, Customer also receives a broader affiliate carve-out, and Vendor competitor assignments are categorically barred rather than governed by consent. The redline is not minimal because it also adds notice, amalgamation, reorganization, sale-of-business, non-delay, suspension, and repricing terms beyond what was necessary for the preferred position. The cross-reference preserves the separate Work restrictions and avoids contradiction with the new assignment carve-outs.
